title.narrative: Improving Resilience to Floods in Polog Region - Comp 1

description.narrative: To address the growing flood-related challenges in the Polog Region and country-wide, and the associated socio-economic consequences, this programme includes a comprehensive set of complementary mitigation and resilience building measures funded by SDC and SECO. These measures, derived from new and existing flood risk assessment studies and plans, will be combined to maximize the benefits for communities and the environment. condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

comment.narrative:
Output 2: 2.1 There is currently no functional flash-flood early warning and public-alter system in place in any part of the country (including Polog). Such a system is being introduced as part of an ongoing UNDP-backed project, covering a limited part of the entire basin area. 2.2 Recent flood events revealed major deficiencies in the response capacity of institutions and communities resulting in casualties and significant damages 2.3 None of the municipalities in the basin have access to comprehensive preparedness plans and response protocols in disastrous situations
Output 3: 3.2 To be defined as part of the FRMP during 2020
Output 4: 4.1 National legislation isn’t harmonized with the objectives of the EU Floods Directive 4.2 Uncoordinated and uninformed investments in flood risk mitigation (to be defined in 2019) due to the lack of national-level strategy and action plan 4.3 Inefficient risk financing mechanisms and limited penetration of insurance product on the market
Outcome 5: 5.1 There is limited knowledge among key personnel of the institutions charged with flood risk management/DRR responsibilities (tbd during preparatory stage) 5.2 Only very limited number of projects in the country are aligned with the contemporary principles of DRR and flood risk management

Outcome 2: -Operationalization of the Early Warning System is ongoing, -Capacity needs assessments of the key institution which will be part of the EWS (branches of the Directorate for Rescue and Protection, Crisis Management Centre, Firefighting brigades, local governments) is ongoing. -Targeted comprehensive trainings for the key institutions in the Polog region is completed. 2 days trainings for urban planning, DRR and climate change, 3 trainings on national flood risk management strategy, 7 training on methodology for risk assessment from different hazards and threats and 1 training on DRR in City of Kraljevo, Serbia. -Providing necessary resources to improve coping capacity of the institutions in-charge (e.g., equipment, material). Different vehicles for local emergency events for Municipality of Gostivar and Tetovo. IT equipment for local emergency agencies in Tetovo and Gostivar. Flood rescue equipment for the Public Communal Enterprises, fire brigades and protection and rescue directorate in Gostivar and Tetovo. -Testing and upgrading the Standard Operating Procedures and protocols for emergency response.-ongoing -Operationalization of the intermunicipal cooperation mechanism for flood risk management on local/regional level. Decision for joint department for water and flood risk is addopted by the councils of the 7 municipalities of the Polog Region. -Strengthening capacities of the Crisis Management Centre Strengthening of the technical capacities with ICT equipment and capacity building workshops. -Public awareness activities to promote the new preparedness approach and the results of the project. Different media materials are prepared and several events on the ongoing and completed activities. -Developing guidance documents, knowledge products and lesson learnt Guide for urban planning, DRR and climate change adoption in urban planning. Outcome 3: -Implement flood structural protection measures, start the Construction of Bogovinjska River. The Construction works on Bogovinjska River are completed. -Develop design documentation to address urban river flooding based in Vardar river in Gostivar and Jegunovce. Design documentation for Vardar river in Gostivar and Jegunovce are completed. -Development of technical documentation for implement flood structural measures in Jagunovce. The technical documentation for implementation of flood structural measured in Jegunovce are completed. -Implement flood structural and bioengineering protection measures in Sipkovica village in Municipality of Tetovo The bioengineering measures in Sipkovica village in Municipality of Tetovo are completed. The flood structural measures are in the final phase of implementation. -Implementation of urban resilience measures in the municipalities of Tetovo and Gostivar as a follow up of the Run-off studies for Gostivar and Tetovo Cleaning of the stormwater network in the City of Gostivar is completed. Afforestation in Sharski vodi for 32 hectars and in Bogovinje for 6 hectars.

Preparedness drill for different institutions. -Gender mainstreaming in different outcomes of the Programme. Update of the Flood Risk Managment Plan. -Publication featuring the results of the project, summary of the key studies, lessons learnt, and recommendation for future actions in the Polog region will be completed in 2023.

Outcome 2: - Full re-activation and upgrade of the monitoring system was impeded by the pandemic situation and small delays resulted in the installation of the meteorological and hydrological monitoring stations. Works were implemented under difficult circumstances considering the harsh conditions at the locations of the monitoring stations, and the need to deal with sensitives stemming from the perceptions of the local communities on the monitoring stations. - The Programme developed detailed requirements for a comprehensive study to improve overall preparedness to floods and other related geohazards in the entire Polog region. The study was launched in the reporting period and the expert team was contracted in August.
Outcome 3: - Shipkovica torrent design is under preparation - Sediment study under preparation - Energy efficient measure implemented in Bogovinje and Tetovo
Outcome 4: - National-level flood risk mitigation strategy outlined
Outcome 5: - Since one of the main objectives of the project is the continuous capacity building of responsible personnel, the Programme continued networking and transfer of knowledge throughout all its components. For example, in order to make best use of experiences so far in the Polog and Southeast planning regions in DRR, the Programme is facilitating exchange between two UNDP-implemented projects (the Polog project funded by the Government of Switzerland and SEE Urban project funded by the EU). The focus on the exchange are the opportunities provided by inter-municipal cooperation in the context of DRR at local level. - Important international/Swiss experience is already being transferred to key beneficiaries through different consultancies and in the course of the stakeholder events (e.g., by the International Technical Adviser, and urban river flooding management experts from Switzerland).

Outcome 2: - Development of the feasibility assessment of preparedness options for Polog region’s municipalities - Develop feasible early warning system based on the experts’ assessment report and overall general preparedness plan for Polog by the end of 2021 - Conceptualizing and piloting a community-based early warning system through involvement of relevant institutions and potentially affected communities.
Outcome 3: - Launching procedure for grants targeting energy efficiency in households in Vrapciste Municipality - Together with the municipalities develop long-term financing instruments to ensure continuity of such feasible solutions for improving energy efficiency of households in the future. - Completing the process of development of the sediment management study and prioritizing the mitigation interventions - Development of detailed technical documentation for selected priority sediment sources and landslides. - Implement sediment control and landslide stabilization measures in identified high risk zones.
Outcome 4: - Facilitation in implementation of the national-level flood risk mitigation strategy and action plan - Facilitate the process of instituting the inter-municipal cooperation mechanism as a permanent administrative body shared by all municipalities
Outcome 5: - Continuation of knowledge and skills development of key institutions through different involvement of relevant staff in different programme activities

Outcome 2: 1. The Overall preparedness study and final assessment of preparedness options for Polog region municipalities was completed. 2. The initial concept for the early warning system was prepared. Following the results from the study and the analysis conducted and presented in the one, will also serve as a starting point in designing the early warning system at regional scale (expected to be delivered at the end of 2022).
Outcome 3: 1. The Municipal Council of Vrapciste already adopted a decision to start with the most feasible solutions for improving energy efficiency of households mostly in rural areas which have limited access to heating options. Financial contribution is also approved by the Council, to be provided from the Municipal Budget. 3. Tendering process for selection of SP for development of design fpr stabilization of 7 landslides is completed, and contracts signed. The selected sites are: Jelovjane, Bozovce, Senokos, Germo, Pirok, Staro Selo, Dolna Lesnica and Pena.
5. In close cooperation with the National Forestry Agency, the Programme supported supply of the irrigation system for the plant nursery in Kumanovo, to provide plants for future reforestation activities. The installation is planned for January 2022.
Outcome 4: 1. The preparation of the national-level flood mitigation strategy and an action plan is in an advanced stage. So far, no prioritization of such needs has been carried out on a national level, i.e. the central government perspective. Besides completing assessments for 7 river basins of the country for which these didn’t exist, the Programme supported application of a consolidated methodology for updating all prior assessments and bringing them to the same level of detail.
2. The Programme continued the support and facilitation the process of institutionalization the inter-municipal cooperation mechanism as a permanent administrative body (Polog Network) shared by all municipalities
Outcome 5: Important international/Swiss experience is already being transferred to key beneficiaries through different consultancies and in the course of the stakeholder events (e.g., by the International Technical Adviser, and urban river flooding management experts from Switzerland). Further continuation of transfer of knowledge will be implemented in the upcoming Case Study for Poroj, where the Programme consultant Mr. Markus Zimmermann will bring knowledge and experience from similar cases in Switzerland.
